_doc: Commands that exist only in onchainos-lite (not in upstream). Merged into the parser surface by core/cli.mjs; excluded from the upstream coverage gate.

doctor.help:
Diagnose the onchainos-lite runtime: Node version, TLS trust store and transport, proxy, hosts to allow in sandboxed environments, API reachability and login state (never prints secrets)

Usage: onchainos doctor [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --offline  Skip the network reachability check
  -h, --help     Print help

auth.help:
Credentials for onchainos-lite: OKX API key (HMAC) auth and encrypted transfer of local credentials to another machine (e.g. a Muse VM)

Usage: onchainos auth <COMMAND>

Commands:
  status    Show which auth mode requests will use (never prints secrets)
  api-key   Store or clear an OKX Web3 API key (key, secret, passphrase)
  transfer  Move credentials to another machine without exposing them in chat
  help      Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

auth status.help:
Show which auth mode requests will use (wallet JWT, API key, anonymous) — never prints secrets

Usage: onchainos auth status

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

auth api-key.help:
Store or clear an OKX Web3 API key (key, secret, passphrase)

Usage: onchainos auth api-key <COMMAND>

Commands:
  set    Store an API key in the encrypted keyring
  clear  Remove the stored API key
  help   Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

auth api-key set.help:
Store an OKX Web3 API key in the encrypted keyring. Values are read from the environment (OKX_API_KEY, OKX_SECRET_KEY, OKX_PASSPHRASE, optional OKX_PROJECT_ID) with --from-env, or from stdin (KEY=VALUE lines or a JSON object with the same names) with --stdin — never from command-line arguments

Usage: onchainos auth api-key set [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --from-env  Read OKX_API_KEY / OKX_SECRET_KEY / OKX_PASSPHRASE / OKX_PROJECT_ID from the environment
      --stdin     Read the same names from stdin (KEY=VALUE lines or JSON)
  -h, --help      Print help

auth api-key clear.help:
Remove the stored API key from the encrypted keyring

Usage: onchainos auth api-key clear

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

auth transfer.help:
Move credentials to another machine (e.g. a Muse VM) without exposing them: the target creates a one-time key, the source seals the credentials to it, the target opens the sealed blob

Usage: onchainos auth transfer <COMMAND>

Commands:
  init  (target) Create a one-time recipient code, valid 30 minutes
  seal  (source) Encrypt local credentials to a recipient code
  open  (target) Decrypt a sealed blob into the local encrypted keyring
  help  Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

auth transfer init.help:
(target machine) Create a one-time X25519 recipient code, valid 30 minutes

Usage: onchainos auth transfer init

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help

auth transfer seal.help:
(source machine) Encrypt local credentials to a recipient code with HPKE (X25519/HKDF-SHA256/AES-256-GCM). Includes the API key when one is configured; --session also moves the wallet login

Usage: onchainos auth transfer seal [OPTIONS] --to <TO>

Options:
      --to <TO>   Recipient code printed by `auth transfer init` on the target
      --session   Also include the wallet login (tokens, session key, wallet list). Use the session on one machine only: the next token refresh invalidates the other copy
      --no-api-key  Do not include the API key
  -h, --help      Print help

auth transfer open.help:
(target machine) Decrypt a sealed blob from `auth transfer seal` into the local encrypted keyring

Usage: onchainos auth transfer open <SEALED>

Arguments:
  <SEALED>  The sealed blob (ocl-seal-v1.…)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help
